question: Question linked to image nº12 A 58-year-old patient with a long-standing heartburn clinic. A high digestive endoscopy is performed, shown in the image. What is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Chronic gastroesophageal reflux -> inflammation of the esophagus -> Barrett's esophagus -> 90% CHAIN: Chronic gastroesophageal reflux -> irritation of the esophagus -> Peptic esophagitis -> 80% CHAIN: Chronic gastroesophageal reflux -> allergic response in the esophagus -> Eosinophilic esophagitis -> 70% CHAIN: Severe vomiting or retching -> tear in the mucosa at the gastroesophageal junction -> Mallory-Weiss disease -> 90%
analysis: Based on the image provided and the clinical history of long-standing heartburn, the most likely diagnosis is peptic esophagitis.
